speaker_role: consultant/marketer (senior consultant at MBA Mission, a paid MBA admissions consulting firm; former journalist and former Columbia alumni interviewer)
commercial_incentive: yes - entire webinar promotes MBA Mission's paid consulting services (comprehensive packages, hourly services, mock interviews) plus affiliated brands (MBA Career Coaching, m7 Financial, JD Mission)
key_insights: This video's content is entirely about graduate MBA/business school admissions (GMAT, business school application rounds, recommenders, waitlists), not US undergraduate admissions, despite the generic 'Admissions Myths Debunked' title.

Addresses MBA-specific myths such as: application round timing (round 1 vs. round 2 are roughly equal, round 3 is a 'shaping round' mainly for distinctive candidates), that a single low grade or GMAT score won't sink an application, and that alumni connections generally don't meaningfully help admission.

Advises taking the GMAT multiple times since schools report only the best score, and that direct supervisors make better recommenders than high-title executives who are less familiar with the applicant's actual work.
Describes waitlist etiquette as sending updates roughly every 3-6 weeks with meaningful news only, and respecting explicit 'do not send additional materials' instructions from closed waitlists.
States the optional essay should be used only to explain specific weaknesses or gaps (e.g., a bad semester, a layoff, an unconventional application detail), not as space for extra generic content.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Cites Wharton's alumni network as roughly 90,000+ and states Harvard's as over 100,000, used to argue alumni recommendations don't meaningfully differentiate applicants (per Rachel Beck, MBA Mission)
States roughly 20% of business school applicants use a recommender other than their direct supervisor (per Rachel Beck)
Cites an unnamed Michigan admissions director's comment that layoffs are viewed sympathetically as part of broader economic conditions, not as a red flag (per Rachel Beck)
notable_or_distinctive: Despite being included as an undergraduate admissions video, this is exclusively about MBA/graduate business school admissions and is not relevant to a US undergraduate admissions knowledge base.
reliability_notes: Off-topic for this knowledge base's focus (US undergraduate admissions) - the entire transcript concerns GMAT/MBA application strategy; relevance score reflects this topical mismatch rather than the quality of the (unverified, promotionally-framed) MBA-specific claims themselves.
